data.gender_notes: Parem is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word ‘परम’ (param) meaning ‘supreme’, ‘beyond’, or ‘transcendental’. In Hindu mythology, Parvati is a goddess associated with love, fertility, and motherhood. The name Parem carries the meaning “Supreme, Beyond” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Parem usually hope their child will grow to embody supreme, beyond and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes transcendence, spiritual growth, and divine love.
data.etymology: Parem belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Supreme, Beyond.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Parem total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.
